title: SpaceX Falcon 9 vehicle page
summary: SpaceX describes Falcon 9 as a reusable two-stage rocket and identifies major reusable-architecture elements including the first stage, Merlin engines, grid fins, landing legs, and fairing reuse.

title: Falcon Payload User's Guide
summary: The 2025 Falcon payload guide documents fault-tolerant avionics/GNC, redundant/triplicated elements, upper-stage Merlin Vacuum, and payload integration interfaces.

title: NASA Crew-2 launch success and first reuse on a crew mission
summary: NASA reported Crew-2 as the first commercial crew mission to reuse both Crew Dragon and Falcon 9 rocket on a crew mission.
limitations: This is one mission milestone, not a full statistical reliability audit.

title: SpaceX Starship vehicle page
summary: SpaceX describes Starship as designed to carry more than 100 metric tonnes to orbit in a fully reusable configuration.
limitations: Official product page; not an independent verification of current operational maturity.

title: SpaceX EU prospectus / investor filing
summary: SpaceX investor filing describes the company's listing context, Starship/Super Heavy architecture claims, and AI compute ambition extending to space. It is used as issuer evidence, not as independent technical validation.
limitations: Issuer filing with forward-looking statements; claims remain unreviewed in the graph.

title: FAA Starship / Super Heavy Boca Chica project page
summary: FAA project page describes SpaceX Starship/Super Heavy launch operations and environmental/license review context for up to 25 annual orbital launches and landings at Boca Chica.
limitations: Reviewed only for Boca Chica site-specific regulatory/environmental and cadence context. Not a global fleet authorization, reliability proof, cost curve, or commercial throughput guarantee.

title: Smithsonian Falcon 9 grid fin collection record
sourceName: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
summary: Smithsonian record explains Falcon 9 first-stage vertical landing, recovery, reuse, and the role of grid fins in reentry control.

title: FCC public notice accepting SpaceX Orbital Data Center system application
summary: FCC notice says SpaceX filed on January 30, 2026 for authority to launch and operate a new NGSO system of up to one million satellites as the SpaceX Orbital Data Center system, primarily relying on optical inter-satellite links and possible Starlink interconnection.
limitations: Reviewed only for the filing/public-notice status and stated NGSO orbital data-center system scope. Not evidence of approval, deployment, technical feasibility, economics, or service maturity.

title: Starlink Technology page: space lasers / optical ISLs
summary: Starlink describes optical inter-satellite links / space lasers as a high-bandwidth space network technology. Used as evidence for Starlink optical-network dependency, not for orbital compute maturity.
limitations: Vendor page; supports network capability context but not a data-center service launch.

title: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology: thermal control
summary: NASA thermal-control chapter explains spacecraft heat balance, thermal radiation, passive/active thermal technologies, deployable radiators, heat pipes, coatings, and small spacecraft thermal constraints.
limitations: Reviewed only for general spacecraft thermal-control constraints and technologies. It does not prove orbital data-center heat rejection at high compute scale.

title: NASA NEPP radiation effects primer
summary: NASA NEPP material explains radiation effects such as total ionizing dose and single-event effects. Used for radiation-risk logic in orbital compute electronics.
limitations: Reviewed only for general space-radiation effects and mitigation need. It does not prove any SpaceX compute board, Starlink system, or orbital data-center payload is radiation-qualified.

title: NASA Spinoff: CubeSats Take a Bus into Space
summary: NASA explains the spacecraft bus concept as the platform providing services such as power, communications, and other spacecraft support functions.
limitations: General spacecraft engineering context, not SpaceX-specific evidence.

title: Rocket Lab launch and space systems capabilities
summary: Rocket Lab public site describes launch and space systems capabilities. Used as public exposure/comparable capability, not as SpaceX supplier evidence.
limitations: Vendor capability page; not a SpaceX supplier confirmation.

title: Redwire space infrastructure capabilities
summary: Redwire public materials describe space infrastructure products and capabilities. Used as public candidate exposure only.
limitations: Not a confirmed SpaceX supplier claim.

title: L3Harris space capabilities
summary: L3Harris public materials describe space systems capabilities. Used as candidate optical/space exposure only.
limitations: Not a confirmed SpaceX supplier claim.

title: Honeywell space electronics
summary: Honeywell public materials describe space electronics capabilities. Used as public candidate exposure only.
limitations: Not a confirmed SpaceX supplier claim.

title: RTX / Blue Canyon Technologies spacecraft platform capabilities
summary: RTX public materials describe Blue Canyon Technologies spacecraft platform capabilities. Used as public bus/platform exposure only.
limitations: Not a confirmed SpaceX supplier claim.

title: NASA Kennedy Space Shuttle Orbiter Thermal Protection System
summary: NASA Kennedy's thermal-protection-system brief describes reusable tile inspection and repair after missions, average tile replacement, silicone adhesive tile bonding to strain-isolator pads, gap control, gap fillers, and rewaterproofing. It supports the bottleneck logic that reusable tile TPS is a maintenance, bonding, inspection, and turnaround process rather than just a material.
limitations: Space Shuttle operational heritage, not Starship-specific hardware, process timing, cost, or reflight acceptance evidence. Used only as independent TPS-process analogue until Starship-specific audited turnaround data exists.
